text: Course-correction on #5409's I2/#34 slicing. Per explicit instruction to verify before assuming #5421's pattern transfers, read the actual code at workspace_agent_target_containment.cpp before touching it for #5422 -- and it doesn't apply: the line-157 inspect checks the WORKSPACE ROOT, the line-208 read reads the TARGET FILE using an identity captured by a wholly separate, earlier inspect_workspace_file() call from a different top-level API entry point, across an async audit-logged tool-call round trip (workspace_agent_session.cpp's preflight/dispatch/read flow). Not a tight pair -- migrating would mean holding a live OS handle open across that whole round trip, worse than the current design, which already does a full before/after identity comparison (link_count included) plus an independent post-read re-walk. Closed #5422 as not-applicable with full reasoning in its closing comment. Re-surveyed every read_physically_contained_file_snapshot() caller in the codebase (not just #5409's originally-named 4 files) and found two genuine tight check-then-read pairs the original triage missed: runtime_pipeline_launcher_artifact_inventory.cpp:129/136 (opened as #5426) and polyglot_supporting_artifact_admission.cpp's admit_polyglot_supporting_artifact():101/114 (opened as #5427 -- explicitly leaving that file's revalidate_polyglot_supporting_artifact_admission() read alone, same admission-to-execution-gap shape as the closed #5422 site). Commented the corrected survey onto #5409. Also finished #5421 itself since last update: PR #5425 merged as 0c1b544c5 after 4 review rounds (round 1 was reviewer-caught, not self-caught -- a real link_count-during-read regression the migration silently dropped; fixed via a shared read_trusted_executable_snapshot() helper; rounds 2-3 added a macro-gated test hook + regression test then fixed it to skip gracefully on hard-link-unsupported filesystems). Issue #5421 closed. Starting #5426 now.
